stories.headline: AI targeting tool linked to US missile strike killing children in Iran
SpaceX Falcon 9 fairing flies for the 40th time, a world first
Tesla's last three new vehicles have no paint shop at all
WSJ says a computer science degree is no longer a golden ticket
$2,700 scholarship helped a young woman build a real welding career

caption:
Here's what happened in AI and tech in the last 24 hours, from a deadly AI-assisted missile strike to a SpaceX reuse record 👇

A Pentagon investigation found that overreliance on Palantir's Maven Smart System, an AI targeting tool, helped cause a US Tomahawk missile strike on an elementary school in Minab, Iran on February 28, killing dozens of civilians, most of them children.

A SpaceX Falcon 9 fairing just flew for the 40th time, the first in SpaceX history to hit that milestone; that nose-cone shell used to get thrown in the ocean after one launch.

Tesla's last three brand-new vehicles, the Semi, the Cybercab, and the Cybertruck, skip liquid paint entirely, using powder coat, injection molding, and bare stainless steel instead.

A computer science degree is no longer a guaranteed path into tech, with AI filling entry-level roles and fewer jobs waiting at the end.

Mikala Sposito got a $2,700 work-ethic scholarship to train as a welder, she gave up Olympic dreams, picked a trade AI can't replace, and built a real career from it.

Sources: Pentagon via Bloomberg, SpaceX, Tesla, Wall Street Journal, Work Ethic Scholarship Foundation
